original.description: A Mauser Gewehr 98 — the German infantry rifle of 1914 — photographed side-on against a plain ground from the collection of the Armémuseum, Stockholm. The museum's own accession label is in frame at the muzzle end; the Commons record for the derivative version notes it was removed there.
original.photographer: Armémuseum (The Swedish Army Museum), Stockholm — the record credits the museum rather than an individual
original.date: catalogued image, uploaded 2015; the object is a Gewehr 98 (adopted 1898)
original.archive: Armémuseum (Swedish Army Museum), Stockholm; object record on DigitaltMuseum, 011024391425; via Wikimedia Commons
original.licence: CC BY 4.0 (Commons record: LicenseShortName "CC BY 4.0"; UsageTerms "Creative Commons Attribution 4.0"; AttributionRequired true). Attribution to Armémuseum is mandatory; there is no share-alike condition on this one.

colorization.status: not colorized, and must not be — a modern colour photograph of the object.

content_policy: ok — a museum object photographed on its own; no casualties
caption: The Mauser Gewehr 98, the rifle the German infantry carried into Belgium: 7.9 mm, five rounds in an internal box magazine, loaded from a charger. Armémuseum, Stockholm.
credit: Photograph: Armémuseum (The Swedish Army Museum), Stockholm, object 011024391425 on DigitaltMuseum, via Wikimedia Commons; CC BY 4.0.
notes: Verified 2026-08-24 against the Commons file record via the MediaWiki API (Artist, Credit, LicenseShortName, UsageTerms, AttributionRequired read from extmetadata). One of four rifle plates photographed by the same museum in the same way — Gewehr 98, Lebel, SMLE, Mauser 1889 — which is what makes them a comparison rather than four pictures of rifles.
